item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is meaningfully preferable because its retry test matches the reported configuration and verifies that the multipart payload is intact on every attempt. Both patches violate the explicit requirement to route Upload through FilesService.Add and both omit source-reader error coverage.","reasons":["B sets RetryAllMethods: true in the 429 test, directly exercising the user-reported POST retry scenario; A does not.","B reads and compares the uploaded content on both the initial request and retry, proving replayability. A only counts requests, so an empty or corrupted replay could pass.","B explicitly tests empty filename and nil content without a request being made.","B parses multipart media parameters and directly checks the field name, filename, and content."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and error behavior instead of calling Add as required.","No tests cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures.","The retry test omits RetryAllMethods: true and does not inspect the body on retried requests."],"risks_b":["Upload also duplicates Add rather than routing the encoded body through it, violating a central maintainability requirement.","No test covers propagation of source-reader failures.","The new Add documentation is extra scope and makes implementation-specific claims about *bytes.Reader/GetBody that are not established by the visible code."]}
